raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Description

Prepare AReaL v2.2.0 from `main`. This PR updates package versions and both lockfiles, points installation and SkyPilot examples to the upcoming v2.2.0 images, and corrects the manual release workflow input example to use the Git tag (`v2.2.0`).

The release scope is all changes on `main` since `v2.1.0`; this PR adds only release metadata.

## Related Issue

None; release preparation.

## Type of Change

Release preparation (`chore`): package metadata and documentation.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/areal-project/community/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (see test details below)
- [x] Relevant local metadata checks pass
- [ ] Documentation updated and built with `./docs/build_all.sh` (content updated; build pending)
- [x] Branch is up to date with `main` at preparation time
- [ ] Self-reviewed via `/review-pr` command
- [x] This PR was created by a coding agent via `/create-pr`
- [ ] This PR is a breaking change

**Breaking Change Details (if applicable):** None in this metadata PR.

## Validation

- `UV_NO_CONFIG=1 UV_OFFLINE=1 UV_PYTHON=<Python 3.12> bash scripts/uv_lock.sh` — passed; both lockfiles regenerated with repository settings.
- `pre-commit run check-added-large-files --files <all 10 changed files>` — passed.
- `UV_NO_CONFIG=1 UV_OFFLINE=1 UV_PYTHON=<Python 3.12> SKIP=check-added-large-files pre-commit run --all-files` — passed. The unmodified all-files run stalled in `git check-attr` inside the large-file hook, so that hook was run separately on all changed files.
- `python areal/tools/check_pyproject_consistency.py` — passed.
- `uv --no-config build --wheel --offline` — produced `areal-2.2.0-py3-none-any.whl`.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

GPU and multi-node training suites were not run locally for this metadata-only PR. Run the release image build and test workflow on the release commit before publishing.

## Additional Context

The v2.2.0 image tags in the docs become available after the GitHub Release triggers the release image workflow. Keep this PR in draft until the release scope and CI are reviewed.
